messages:
incident-bot: Paging @alyssa (oncall) — alert: model-quality-regression for model redwood-qa-v2 (error rate +35% on top-1 rerank, 13 customer complaints in last 10m). Links: https://observability.redwood/alerts/174. Priority: P1, page triggered by customer-impact rule. :rotating_light:

alyssa (oncall): On it. jumping in now. any immediate mitigation recommended?

matt (sre): Looking at prod metrics — tokens/sec OK, latencies normal. Error signal is QA regression metric (eval harness flagged spike after 2025-11-02T03:12 deploy). Deployment id: deploy-2025-11-02-03-12-models. I can pull logs, ETA 2m.

jess (ml-eng): I just saw the model rollout. Canary passed but rollout to 100% started 03:15. Quick check: model redwood-qa-v2-int4. There was an attempted kernel change on the runtime for a performance patch. Might have changed attention rounding that affects scoring.

sam (support): customers complaining about hallucinated rerank results in search product; some have included examples. Major affected tenant is customer-acme (support ticket #4321). They asked if this is an ongoing issue.

alyssa (oncall): Ok triage plan: 1) Assess customer impact and post interim status page 2) If regression confirmed, rollback model to previous pinned version (redwood-qa-v1.9) across hosted & dedicated 3) Notify CS + customers with templated message. Who can execute rollback?

matt (sre): I can run rollback for hosted; need eng-platform help for Dedicated pool pin. Rollback command for hosted is below (run from ops-ctl):
```
ops-ctl model rollback --model redwood-qa-v2 --to redwood-qa-v1.9 --reason "quality regression after 2025-11-02 deploy"
```
I will queue it once we agree.

jess (ml-eng): Confirmed regression on our internal eval set. Metrics: BLEU-like rerank delta -0.18, factuality down 22%. Looks like quantization path change. Recommend rollback to v1.9 and pin that version while we debug kernel change. Also add a throttle rule to block auto-rollout for model family until patch is validated.

leo (product): For customer communications we should be explicit about impact and mitigation timeline. Sam, can you prep the status page + customer note; I'll review. We should avoid deep technical details.

sam (support): Drafting now. Proposed statuspage update (short form):
```
Component: Redwood Generation API (model redwood-qa-v2)
Status: Degraded performance
Impact: A subset of text reranking requests may return lower-quality results for some customers (affecting search and retrieval features).
Current status: Investigating. Working on rollback to a prior model version to restore quality. Next update within 30 minutes.
```
Will publish after review.

alyssa (oncall): Go ahead and publish the status update as a first notice, tag customers with active incidents. Use statuspage-bot to publish and include link back to this thread.

statuspage-bot: Draft published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-02-qa-regression-draft — awaiting confirmation from leo / alyssa.

leo (product): Slight wording tweak: change "degraded performance" to "degraded output quality". Sam update and publish.

sam (support): Updated and publishing now. Published link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-02-qa-regression

sam (support) (edited): Customer notification template (for affected tenants):
```
Subject: Temporary quality regression affecting some rerank requests — we are rolling back
Hi <Customer name>,

Were reaching out because you may have seen reduced quality for some reranking/search results starting at ~03:12 UTC. Our monitoring detected a regression after a recent model rollout. We are rolling back the model to the previously stable version and expect full recovery within ~15-30 minutes.

What were doing: Rolling back the model and pinning the stable version while we investigate. We will follow up with a post-incident report.

No action required from you. If you see anything after the rollback, please reply to this thread or open a ticket referencing #4321.

Apologies for the disruption,
Redwood Support
```

jess (ml-eng): I recommend adding a short internal template for runtime teams to pin the model across Dedicated and Private (commands):
```
# Hosted rollback (ops-ctl)
ops-ctl model rollback --model redwood-qa-v2 --to redwood-qa-v1.9

# Dedicated: update routing policy to pin old model (k8s config snippet)
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/redwood-dedicated-routing MODEL_PIN=redwood-qa-v1.9

# Private customers: provide runbook snippet and ask their infra contact to apply
```

alyssa (oncall): Matt, proceed with hosted rollback once sam confirms statuspage published. Jess, can you coordinate Dedicated pin with eng-platform and notify private customers list?

matt (sre): Starting hosted rollback now. Command output:
```
[2025-11-02T03:28:12Z] ops-ctl: initiating rollback...
[2025-11-02T03:28:30Z] ops-ctl: 35% -> draining in-flight requests
[2025-11-02T03:29:02Z] ops-ctl: 100% -> rollback complete. active model: redwood-qa-v1.9
```

jess (ml-eng): Got confirmation from eng-platform: Dedicated routing policy updated and pinned to redwood-qa-v1.9 across pools in us-west/us-east. Private deploy customers notified via their AMs.

incident-bot: Note: customer-acme ticket #4321 marked 'mitigated' by sam (support).

alyssa (oncall): Observability shows quality metrics recovering. Internal eval delta returning to baseline within 6 minutes. Marking incident from 'investigating' -> 'mitigated' in our tracker. Sam/leo please publish follow-up message to customers that rollback is complete and provide ETA for postmortem.

sam (support): Published status update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-02-qa-regression#update-1 — message says rollback complete, customers may see intermittent artifacts for up to 10 minutes.

leo (product): Customer message (final):
```
Hi <Customer name>,

Update: We completed a rollback of the recently deployed model and quality has been restored. You should see normal results now; if you notice anything else please let us know. Were preparing a post-incident report with root cause and follow-up mitigations, including pinning and stricter rollout gating for the model family.

Thanks for your patience,
Redwood Product & Support
```

alyssa (oncall): Handing off to jess/matt for RCA and postmortem. Oncall clear in 30m unless any regressions reoccur. Good job team. :tada:

jess (ml-eng): Action items created:
- [ ] Root cause: quantify kernel perf/quantization divergence & revert patch if needed
- [ ] Add rollout gating: require canary evaluation on top-1/rerank metrics before 50% rollouts
- [ ] Add automated pin-on-degraded rule to prevent auto-rollout until signoff
- [ ] Postmortem draft by 2025-11-03 17:00 UTC

matt (sre): Ops actions: audit recent runtime kernel changes, add canary-only flag to kernel flip for next deploy, document rollback steps in runbook.

statuspage-bot: Incident status updated to "resolved" on status page at 2025-11-02T03:38:40Z.

incident-bot: Closing page for oncall. If anything re-occurs, it will re-open.

leo (product): Recommend we include a short internal comms template for execs (one-liner + impact) to be used next time. I'll drop a draft in #product-briefs.

sam (support): Customer follow-ups posted to ticket #4321 and affected tenant list. Closing with customers.

alyssa (oncall): Closing thread. Thanks all.

(edited)
